dailyTip.title: Know Your Rights
dailyTip.description: A new legal insight delivered every day. Scroll through expert tips on Indian law.
dailyTip.tipOf: Tip {{current}} of {{total}} — A new tip is featured daily. All information is for general awareness only and does not constitute legal advice.

tips.tip: You have the right to remain silent during police questioning. Under Article 20(3) of the Constitution, no person accused of an offence can be compelled to be a witness against themselves.
Under the RTI Act 2005, you can request information from any public authority within 30 days. For matters involving life or liberty, the response must come within 48 hours.
Every arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest. This is a fundamental right under Article 22(2) of the Constitution.
If you're a victim of a crime, you can file a Zero FIR at any police station regardless of jurisdiction. The station is then required to transfer it to the appropriate station.
Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, you can file a complaint about defective goods or deficient services without a lawyer through the Consumer Forum.
The Domestic Violence Act 2005 protects not just wives but also sisters, mothers, and daughters living in the same household from physical, verbal, and economic abuse.
As a tenant, you cannot be evicted without proper notice as specified in your rental agreement or state rent laws. Sudden eviction by a landlord is illegal.
Under the Factories Act, workers are entitled to overtime wages at twice the ordinary wage rate for work beyond normal working hours.
Any citizen can challenge a law or government action violating Fundamental Rights by filing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) directly in the High Court or Supreme Court.
Under POCSO Act, any person who suspects child sexual abuse is legally bound to report it to the police or Special Juvenile Police Unit. Non-reporting is itself an offence.
Every person is entitled to free legal aid in India, regardless of income, if they're accused in a case where imprisonment is possible.
Under the Hindu Succession Act, daughters have equal rights to ancestral property as sons — even if they were born before the 2005 amendment to the Act.

quiz.title: Legal Quiz
quiz.description: Test your knowledge of Indian law. Questions covering constitutional rights, landmark judgments, and more.
quiz.question: Question {{current}} of {{total}}
quiz.scored: You scored {{score}} out of {{total}} questions correctly.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Life and Personal Liberty guaranteed?
questions.explanation: Article 21 guarantees that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

questions.question: Which act governs the protection of children from sexual offences in India?
questions.explanation: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 specifically deals with sexual crimes against children.

questions.question: What is the maximum period a person can be detained under preventive detention without the approval of an Advisory Board?
questions.explanation: Under Article 22(4), a person can be detained for a maximum of 3 months without board approval.

questions.question: The Right to Information (RTI) Act was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The RTI Act was enacted in 2005. It empowers citizens to seek information from any public authority.

questions.question: Which body is responsible for making recommendations for appointments to the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: The Collegium System, comprising the Chief Justice of India and the 4 most senior judges, makes binding recommendations.

questions.question: Under Indian law, what is the minimum age for a valid marriage for a woman?
questions.explanation: Currently the minimum marriage age for women is 18 years under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'Untouchability' in any form and makes its practice a punishable offence.

questions.question: The concept of 'Basic Structure Doctrine' was established in which landmark case?
questions.explanation: The Basic Structure Doctrine was established in the Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) case.
